subject: Medford Vocational Technical High School Programs
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed electrical teacher Rich Cormio regarding the expansion, curriculum, and community initiatives of Medford Vocational Technical High School.

items.title: Introduction and Teaching Career
items.summary: John Petrella interviewed Rich Cormio about his 18-year career teaching at the Medford Vocational Technical High School (MVTHS) after 30 years in the electrical trade.

items.title: Evolution of Vocational Education
items.summary: Cormio described the growth of the school from 60 to over 200 annual graduates and the shift in public perception regarding the value of trade education.

items.title: Freshman Exploratory and Admissions
items.summary: Freshmen rotate through 15 programs to sample different trades before selecting a specialty, with admissions based on attendance, behavior, and interest.

items.title: Co-op Program and Trade Partnerships
items.summary: The senior co-op program allows students to work professionally for local companies and unions on alternating weeks to earn wages and trade hours.

items.title: College Pathways and Credits
items.summary: Cormio clarified that MVTHS graduates earn standard high school credits and can pursue higher education, with some colleges waiving language requirements for vocational students.

items.title: Promotional Presentation
items.summary: A video segment featured Director Chad Fallon discussing technical skills and the potential for a future building project to expand community opportunities.

items.title: Community Projects and Services
items.summary: Students collaborate across shops to provide community services, including building pre-fabricated sheds and constructing accessibility ramps for residents in need.

items.title: Vocational Shop Overview
items.summary: Cormio reviewed various specialized programs, including biotech, licensed cosmetology, and a student-run restaurant that is open to the public for lunch.
